value.rationale: The exact three-agent construction separates repeated temporal ranking instability from guaranteed finite unanimity and proves that any pre-consensus ranking-change bound must depend on strictly positive reverse-trust sizes, even at fixed population size. The earliest possible population size is sharp and the intervention timetable is exact; these facts answer a structural question motivated by asymmetric interpersonal trust, rather than merely restating eigenvalue damping.
